note: Hand-written viva questions about the bundled sample repo. Each has a strong, a vague and a wrong answer. A good grader must rank strong > vague > wrong. The 'injection' answers try to talk the grader into a high score and must score 0.

cases.question: What happens in create_short_link when the random code you generate is already taken?
expected_points: store.save raises DuplicateCodeError for a taken code
the loop catches it and tries a new random code
it gives up after MAX_ATTEMPTS (5) and raises RuntimeError

answers.strong: save() in the store raises DuplicateCodeError if the code already exists. create_short_link catches that inside the for loop and just generates another random code. It tries MAX_ATTEMPTS times, which is 5, and if every attempt collides it raises RuntimeError, which the API layer turns into a 503.
answers.vague: It checks if the code is unique and if not it makes another one. There is some limit on how many times it tries.
answers.wrong: It appends a counter to the URL and hashes it again with md5 until the hash is unique, so it never fails.

cases.question: If the same user shortens the same URL twice, what do they get back and why?
expected_points: find_by_url looks up the existing code for that owner and url
the existing code is returned instead of creating a new one
the lookup is per owner, so two different users get different codes

answers.strong: Before generating anything it calls store.find_by_url with the url and the owner_id. The store keeps a dict keyed by (owner_id, url), so if this user already shortened that url the existing code is returned and nothing new is saved. Because the key includes the owner, a different user shortening the same url gets their own new code.
answers.vague: It probably returns the same link because it checks the database first, I think.
answers.wrong: They get a new code every time because codes are random, the old one is overwritten.

cases.question: Explain how TokenBucket.allow decides whether a request goes through.
expected_points: _refill adds tokens based on elapsed time times refill_per_second
if tokens are below cost it returns False, otherwise it subtracts cost and returns True

answers.strong: allow first calls _refill, which works out how much time passed since the last check and adds elapsed times refill_per_second tokens, capped at capacity. If the bucket has fewer tokens than the cost it returns False and the API sends a 429. Otherwise it subtracts the cost, stores the new count with the current clock time and returns True.
answers.vague: It is a rate limiter, it allows some number of requests and blocks the rest.
answers.wrong: It counts requests in a fixed one-minute window and resets the counter to zero at the start of every minute.

cases.question: What stops one user from disabling another user's link, and what does the API return in each case?
expected_points: disable compares record.owner_id with the caller's owner_id
a mismatch raises PermissionError, which handle_disable turns into 403
a missing code returns False, which becomes 404

answers.strong: store.disable loads the record and compares record.owner_id with the owner_id passed in. If they differ it raises PermissionError, and handle_disable catches that and returns 403 forbidden. If the code doesn't exist at all disable returns False and the handler returns 404. Only the owner gets a 200 and the record's disabled flag set to True.
answers.vague: There is an ownership check so only the owner can disable it, otherwise it gives an error.
answers.wrong: Any logged-in user can disable a link, the API just checks that user_id is not empty and then deletes the link from the store.

cases.question: Which URLs does validate_url reject, and why might each rule be there?
expected_points: rejects any scheme other than http or https
rejects URLs with no host (empty netloc)
raises InvalidURLError, which the API returns as 400

answers.strong: It strips the url and parses it with urlparse. Anything whose scheme is not http or https is rejected, which blocks things like javascript: or file: links. It also rejects a url with no netloc, so no host, and anything over 2048 characters. Each case raises InvalidURLError and handle_create returns that message with a 400.
answers.vague: It validates the URL format and throws an error if it is invalid.
answers.wrong: It sends a HEAD request to the URL and rejects it if the site returns a 404.

cases.question: What does resolve do with a link that has been disabled?
expected_points: returns None when the record is missing or disabled
clicks are only incremented for live links

answers.strong: resolve gets the record and returns None if it is missing or record.disabled is True, so handle_redirect answers 404 and the user can't tell a disabled link from one that never existed. The increment_clicks call comes after that check, so clicks are only counted for live links.
answers.wrong: It still redirects but shows a warning page first, and the click is counted either way.
